title: How to Tell A Story
subtitle: The finest jokes are told gravely.

items.text: How to Tell A Story

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Hello, Fingers.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: MacGuffin the Knife—I've found him.
The Headonion Show

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Joining us today is someone who experienced this bizarre incident firsthand. Please welcome Miss Mercuria!

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Mercuria, it's true you've located the fabled stash of gold, MacGuffin the Knife, correct?

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Could you share with us how you managed to find him, in the flesh?

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Mm-hmm?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: It was a sunny day.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: The day that I met Fingers for the first time. We shared a sandwich on the street.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Back then, he was just a kid studying literature at community college.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: But when he visited his mother on her sickbed with a letter of withdrawal and placed it on her velvet pillow ...

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: She kicked him out the next day.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: After I get out, I'm heading north.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: That's what he said.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: North's the place to be. Tons of cash to be made and the kind of life my **** parents could never imagine.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: The whole scene's thriving, and every shiny little thing you've ever wanted is right there for the taking.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Not even a complete dumbass pictures a future for himself behind these bars fighting over who gets to watch an old TV.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: But for him, that TV was the only link he had to modern culture while he was locked away.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Not that there's ever anything good on. Most of the time, it's nothing but ads.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Over time, those ads changed him. They gave him an entirely new way of seeing the world.
The greatest "achievement" of consumerism is how it reduces the value of our lives.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: It's all about the labels you wear and what you spent to get them, that's how you measure your success against everyone else, and the winner tears the loser's world to shreds.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: If I had money, all the money I needed, I'd buy all the things I've seen in shop windows and TV ads.
That's the motive of television commercials: to convince you that they're selling the life that has been denying you.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: All I'm doing is taking back what's rightfully mine.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: That's the only way you can call me someone who's legit and untouchable.
Visiting Room

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Hello, Fingers.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: MacGuffin the Knife—I've found him.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: You found him?

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: You mean you got it?!

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: The dog?! The one the boss would walk along the waterfront five friggin' times a day?!

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I found him.
Every word that comes out of her mouth flows as effortlessly as grabbing a drive-thru meal on a Sunday evening.
She never realizes the weight behind her words; she strings them together like ribbons in the wind.
Seemingly unconcerned with their aftermath.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: So, go on tell me!

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: He was fifty miles south of Sugartown, out in the boondocks.
More accurately, he was stuck in the crevice of a large stone at an abandoned campsite.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Alright, so where do you get it now?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Right here.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Only thing I can see here is you and me.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: They didn't let me bring him into the visiting room.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: So, what you're telling me is, right now, MacGuffin the Knife is ...
All it takes is a little imagination to picture that, at that moment, the world's most valuable puppy is playing dominoes with the prison guards.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I'll hold onto him until you're out.
Fingers fixes Mercuria with a sharp, rodent-like glint in his eyes.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Alright. Alright.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: So, go on, tell me, how'd you two ... I mean, you ... manage to find it?
The girl stays quiet, her eyes narrowing as she holds Fingers's gaze.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Eh?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: How about you tell me where my companion is?

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: What? What are you talking about?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: My partner, Pickles. He was taken by your man last night. I'd like to know why.
Fingers cracks his knuckles, each one making a sharp "click-clack" sound.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Yeah, should've figured you'd catch wise that I gave the order.
A charged silence hangs in the air.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: That was a mistake.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: It's corrupting your energy, clouding it with impurities.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: It's already so different now from how it was back then.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Watch out. Energy like that comes with a heavy price, one you may not want to pay.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Man, back when I met you, making threats wasn't even in your playbook.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: The first rule of surviving on the streets: trust no one, and always keep a card up your sleeve.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: I assumed you knew how these things worked by now.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Once you found out where the dog was, how was I to know you'd hand it over and not keep it for yourself?
His words stir up a hint of déjà vu.
The streets, the trash heaps, half-eaten sandwiches, and blood banks ... the life she lived along her journey.
Mercuria blinks her eyes.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Maybe it is.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: But that isn't how I work.
Fingers's face twitches with a sudden buried emotion.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Pfft. Hahahaha!

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: I gotta say, Mercuria, sometimes you come off like you're too innocent for this world, but then you'll flip, and it's like I'm dealing with a stone-cold killer.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: You seem like you've cracked the code on spinning those ironic little tales of yours.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Mark Twain said it best: "The humorous story depends for its effect upon the manner of the telling ..."

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: "The humorous story is told gravely; the teller does his best to conceal the fact that he even dimly suspects that there is anything funny about it."
Waxing poetic during a crisis is the signature of a second-rate literary nerd.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Let's be real. In this situation, you can't back out. You've gotta say yes, whether you like it or not.

items.speaker: Fingers
items.text: Tomorrow night, seven sharp, Black Iron Forest near the prison. Bring it here, and we'll wrap this up.
Unfortunately, Mark Twain really did say those words.
